correctness.rationale: A triple fails precisely when a cyclic gap is at least n/2, because the complementary arc then contains the triple and is a shortest path, including ties. Any four vertices have two complementary two-gap arcs, one at most n/2 and hence containing a forbidden triple. Therefore C_3=0. For the positive ranges, balanced gaps g_i satisfy ceil(n/3)+1<n/2 at n=9 and n=12 and the slack is nondecreasing in steps of two; the gaps are also at least two. All eight transversals of three adjacent pairs therefore have positive gaps strictly below n/2. Their alternating chain is a nonzero 2-cycle since dropping any vertex cancels the two binary choices at that position. A coefficient +/-1 yields a map H_2->Z sending that class to a generator, proving primitivity. At each excluded order, listing positive triples of gaps below n/2 gives the frozen table. For n=7 an edge of gap 1 supports (1,3,3) uniquely; then a gap-3 edge supports (2,2,3) uniquely. At n=10 a gap-2 edge supports (2,4,4) uniquely; then a gap-4 edge supports (3,3,4) uniquely. The one-phase rows each have the indicated unique supporting edge. These removals leave no triangles. The final sentence about second-phase edges having 'no cofaces' after phase one is a local wording slip: they have exactly one remaining triangular coface, as the table and uniqueness argument require. This does not change the proved classification.
residual_risks: The finite ranks check the onset region but do not establish the whole family; the balanced-gap cycle supplies the universal positive direction. No full Betti-number or homotopy classification is asserted.
